memory_candidates.content: In scripts/check-module-invariants.sh's C23 naming-exemption block, the three exemption mechanisms are keyed at different granularities: UPPER_ALLOW and SHADOW_ALLOW key on the bare declaration/base name and apply tree-wide to all current and future occurrences of that name, while FROZEN_PREFIX keys on a path prefix and only exempts pairs with a member under it. A SHADOW_ALLOW entry for a base name disables detection for that entire name bucket permanently, not just the measured pairs -- so it silently absorbs any future accidental collision on the same name. Worth checking this distinction before adding any exemption entry to a similarly-shaped naming/shadowing linter.

check-module-invariants.sh's C23 outer-shadows-inner shadow-pair report truncates its printed list to shadow[:10] while the FAIL count reflects the true total, so a count of 11 or more can hide rows entirely absent from the printed output. Re-run from a scratch copy with the print cap lifted (or cross-check the printed count against the FAIL header) before treating the printed list as exhaustive.
